relevance_note: Case report of one Danon disease patient with a printed variant: 'The diagnosis of Danon disease was made on the basis of genetic testing (c.877C > T in exon 7)'.
method_note: Read the paper fully by hand; a Python script in the scratch directory assembled the JSON and cut Table 2 and Table 1 row spans from the Markdown (checked against the tables). Scope: the index patient; his mother (died of suspected dilated cardiomyopathy) and younger sister (dilated-phase hypertrophic cardiomyopathy) as affected relatives with no variant rows (not tested per paper). The 'healthy aunt' is neither tested nor affected and gets no row. Table 2 (patients as columns; column headers: 1 'This case', 2-3 'Boucek et al. [3]', 4-5 'Sugie et al. [4]', 6-7 'Kitahara et al. [5]', 8-9 'Maron et al. [6]', 10 'Lacoste-Collin et al. [8]'): columns 2-5 and 8 are group summaries (counts/means) and get no rows; columns 6, 7, 9, 10 are single individuals with individual-level data and get rows labelled 'Table 2 column k'. Column 1 'This case' is the index patient, labelled 'patient'. Kitahara columns 6 and 7 share a merged Sex cell '2 females'; each is recorded as female. '–' cells (undefined symbol) and 'NA' are not reported. Table 2 legend defines Yes/No for individuals; quoted with 'No' cells. Disease label for literature patients left 'not reported' (table title does not name the disease per patient). No variants printed for literature patients. The gene is printed as 'LAMP-2' only in the Discussion; the variant sentence does not name the gene. No transcript, protein change, zygosity, inheritance or classification given. Contradictions/oddities: Table 2 gives the index patient's age at onset as 23 (first heart failure), while the text describes a workup at 13 for short stature and enzyme elevation; onset recorded as the table states. Table 1 LVDD before discharge 55 mm vs text 57 mm after implantation (not used). Lacoste-Collin column: age at diagnosis 36 but age at HTX 28 (recorded as printed). 'No' for WPW syndrome (index patient) is not treated as excluding the broader pre-excitation checklist item; 'No' intellectual disability does not exclude the composite cognitive item. 'No' myopathy was taken to exclude 'proximal muscle weakness (skeletal myopathy)'. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy was taken as left ventricular hypertrophy; 'dilated-phase' for the sister was taken as dilated left ventricle. 'organic abnormalities' (excluded) is written as the paper does; it names no specific finding. Mother's DCM is 'suspected' (recorded as observed with the qualifier; checklist left not reported).
